chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who prays four Rak'at, reciting in every Rak'at 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' fifty times, will not finish (complete his prayer), and there will be a sin (remaining) between him and Allah.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Say, He is Allah, One - Surah 112)
key_terms.لَمْ يَنْفَتِلْ: Did not finish/wrap up (implying incompleteness or lingering effect)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and significance of praying four Rak'at with fifty recitations of Surah Al-Ikhlas in each Rak'at?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kadhi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) prescribes a specific voluntary prayer of four Rak'at, emphasizing the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas fifty times per unit. The phrase 'a sin remains between him and Allah' is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating that while the act is highly meritorious and expiates many sins, it does not constitute a complete absolution of all minor faults, thereby encouraging consistent devotion rather than treating it as a singular 'get-out-of-jail-free' card.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Barqy, from Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who prays a Salāt of four Rak’at, reciting in every Rak’at [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112) fifty times, would not wrap up (finish), and there would be a sin (remaining) between him and Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy from Sa‘dan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “He has narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a Hadith with the text which is the same as that of the previous Hadith.”
